purpose: Ramelteon is used to help people who have trouble falling asleep. It is approved for long-term use and is especially helpful for people who lie awake a long time before drifting off. Unlike some other sleep medications, it is not a controlled substance.
how_it_works: Your brain has a built-in sleep clock that relies on a natural hormone called melatonin to tell your body it is time to sleep. Ramelteon works by mimicking melatonin and binding to the same receptors in your brain that melatonin does. This helps signal to your body that it is nighttime and time to fall asleep.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include drowsiness or sleepiness the next day, dizziness, tiredness, and nausea. Some people may also notice headaches. These effects are usually mild.
warnings: Do not take Ramelteon if you are also taking a medication called Fluvoxamine (used for depression or OCD), as this combination can be dangerous. Avoid alcohol while taking this medication. Tell your doctor if you have liver problems, since this drug is processed by the liver. In rare cases, it can affect hormone levels, so let your doctor know if you notice unusual changes like missed periods, breast tenderness, or decreased sex drive. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery until you know how it affects you.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 8 mg taken by mouth about 30 minutes before bedtime. Take it on an empty stomach or with only a light snack for best results, as a heavy meal can slow down how well it works. Only take it when you are ready to go to sleep and have enough time for a full night's rest.
